land.text: Ottoman Palestine west of the Jordan, run by the Occupied Enemy Territory Administration until the civil administration of July 1920

predecessors.note: The Mandatory Palestine infobox gives the 'Occupied Enemy Territory Administration' as the state's predecessor; Cliopatria has no OETA row. The east bank (Transjordan) is not part of this dossier: kingdom-of-jordan founds the Emirate there in April 1921 from nobody's land.

land.text: Israel 'expand[ed] to encompass about 78% of the territory of the former British Mandate' (Mandatory Palestine page)
the West Bank, 'Transjordan seizing and subsequently annexing the West Bank'

successors.note: Annexed formally on 24 April 1950 (kingdom-of-jordan dossier); held from May 1948 as occupation of the 'palestinians' shape.

land.text: the Gaza Strip, 'the Kingdom of Egypt seizing the Gaza Strip' which 'established' the All-Palestine Protectorate

capitals.name: Jerusalem
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Jerusalem'. High Commissioner's seat: Augusta Victoria on Mount Scopus until 1933, then the new building at Armon HaNetziv until the end of British rule in 1948.

correction.text: Palestine west of the Jordan: the modern Israel and Palestine without the Golan Heights, which the 1920 Franco-British convention left in the French sphere ('The bulk of the Golan Heights was placed in the French sphere'); the Sea of Galilee shore and 20 villages still French-administered until the 1923 settlement

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Mandate row). Civil administration from July 1920 ('In July 1920, a British civilian administration headed by a High Commissioner replaced the military administration'). Area of the named shape about 24,300 km2 by cells against the infobox 25,585.3 km2 (no year) and 26,625.6 km2 'as of 1931': ratio 0.91-0.95, within the factor of two. The east bank is not drawn: the 16 September 1922 memorandum put Transjordan outside the Palestine mandate and kingdom-of-jordan carries it from April 1921.

correction.text: Palestine as the League of Nations Council put it in force on 29 September 1923: west of the Jordan, northern frontier at the Paulet-Newcombe line (Mediterranean to Al-Hamma) which 'include[d] the entire Sea of Galilee and the Yarmuk valley'; the east bank is Transjordan

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The 7 March 1923 approval adds the Sea of Galilee, the Yarmuk valley and 20 villages to Palestine (gain event); the shape is otherwise the 1920-22 shape, since the pages opened record no other change of frontier to 1947. Southern frontier with Sinai and the Wadi Araba line were not opened (Transjordan memorandum quotes the Order-in-Council line 'two miles west of the town of Akaba' up the Wadi Araba, Dead Sea and Jordan to the Yarmuk).

correction.text: the Mandate until it 'expired' at midnight 14/15 May 1948; British troops 'essentially withdrawn' and the land already contested between the Yishuv and the Arab side since 30 November 1947

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1 January to 14 May 1948. The 1948 Palestine war page does not date the last British troop departure ('page silent'); the map should draw the shape through May and let the successors' found and occupation events take the land (state-of-israel found 14 May 1948; kingdom-of-jordan occupation of the West Bank; Egypt in Gaza).

region.text: Palestine west of the Jordan: the land of Ottoman Palestine under British occupation, Jerusalem as capital

ledger.note: July 1920: a British civilian administration under a High Commissioner takes over Palestine. 'In July 1920, a British civilian administration headed by a High Commissioner replaced the military administration'; Herbert Samuel 'arrived in Palestine on 20 June 1920 to take up his appointment from 1 July'; the mandate was assigned at San Remo ('Mandate assigned: 25 April 1920', infobox) and took effect formally on 29 September 1923.

region.text: the Sea of Galilee and the Yarmuk valley, with 20 formerly French-administered villages, brought into Palestine by the Paulet-Newcombe line (Mediterranean to Al-Hamma); Banias and the bulk of the Golan stay French

ledger.note: 7 March 1923: the Franco-British frontier is settled. The Paulet-Newcombe agreement 'was approved with some caveats by the French and British governments on 7 March 1923'; the 1922 commission amendments moved the northern boundary to 'include the entire Sea of Galilee and the Yarmuk valley', and '20 villages which had previously been under French administration were incorporated into Palestine'. Mandate in force 29 September 1923.

region.text: the Jewish state of the partition plan and the ground it won, about 78% of the Mandate by the 1949 armistice lines (the page gives no date for the gains beyond the war)

ledger.note: 14/15 May 1948: Israel takes most of the Mandate. 'At midnight on 14/15 May 1948, the Mandate for Palestine expired, and the State of Israel came into being'; Israel was to 'expand to encompass about 78% of the territory of the former British Mandate' by the 1949 armistices.

region.text: the West Bank, 'Transjordan seizing and subsequently annexing the West Bank'

ledger.note: May 1948: Transjordan takes the West Bank. The page says Transjordan seized and 'subsequently annex[ed]' it; no day is given (the 1948 Palestine war page: Transjordan armistice 3 April 1949).

region.text: the Gaza Strip, seized by the Kingdom of Egypt

ledger.note: May 1948: Egypt takes the Gaza Strip. 'the Kingdom of Egypt seizing the Gaza Strip', which the page says 'established' the All-Palestine Protectorate; the page gives no day (Egypt-Israel armistice 24 February 1949, 1948 Palestine war page).

region.text: the whole Mandate territory at its end

ledger.note: 14/15 May 1948: the Mandate ends. 'At midnight on 14/15 May 1948, the Mandate for Palestine expired, and the State of Israel came into being' (infobox: End of Mandate 14 May 1948; the legal-instrument page: in force '29 September 1923 to 15 May 1948'). Land passes to Israel, to Transjordan (West Bank) and to Egypt (Gaza).

wars.name: 1948 Palestine war

zones.text: the whole of former Mandatory Palestine: the West Bank including East Jerusalem, the Negev and the Gaza coast, the Galilee and the Jordan Valley salients

wars.outcome: The civil war phase began on 30 November 1947 after the UN partition resolution of 29 November (33 to 13, 10 abstentions); the Mandate ended at midnight 14/15 May 1948 and 'the surrounding Arab armies invaded Palestine' the next morning. Armistices: Egypt 24 February, Lebanon 23 March, Transjordan 3 April, Syria 20 July 1949; Israel held about 78% of Mandatory Palestine, Transjordan the West Bank, Egypt Gaza.
wars.note: The Mandate government was not a combatant of the 1948 war after its end; 'The British had essentially withdrawn their troops' (date of the last departure: page silent). The 1936-1939 Arab revolt and the 1944-1948 Jewish insurgency against the Mandate were not opened (page budget) and are not listed.

certainty.note: The northern frontier was the 23 December 1920 convention line with a joint commission still to mark it; the 'Sea of Galilee' crossing and the Golan were disputed until 1923; the Transjordan limit was settled only on 16 September 1922.

Frontier fixed by the Paulet-Newcombe line of 7 March 1923 in the north and the Order-in-Council line 'up the centre of the Wady Araba, Dead Sea and River Jordan to its junction with the River Yarmuk' in the east; the Sinai/Negev frontier with Egypt was not opened and may be softer.

sources.title: Mandatory Palestine
sources.note: Identity, infobox (25 April 1920 assignment, 29 September 1923, 14 May 1948, 25,585.3 km2, 26,625.6 km2 in 1931), July 1920 civil administration, capital and High Commissioners, the end of the Mandate and what Israel, Transjordan and Egypt took. Page silent on the San Remo date, the Transjordan memorandum date, Paulet-Newcombe and OETA dates.

sources.title: Transjordan memorandum
sources.note: Approved by the League of Nations Council on 16 September 1922: Britain administers the land west of the Jordan as Palestine; Transjordan self-government May 1923; the eastern boundary line.

sources.title: 1948 Palestine war
sources.note: 30 November 1947 civil war; termination of the Mandate at midnight 14 May 1948; the 1949 armistices (24 Feb, 23 Mar, 3 Apr, 20 Jul); Israel about 78% of Mandatory Palestine.

sources.title: Paulet-Newcombe Agreement
sources.note: The 1920 convention (23 December 1920) and the 7 March 1923 approval of the northern frontier; the Sea of Galilee, the Yarmuk valley and 20 villages added to Palestine; Golan and Banias French.

sources.title: Mandate for Palestine (legal instrument)
sources.note: San Remo April 1920; Council confirmation 22/24 July 1922; in force 29 September 1923 to 15 May 1948; Article 25 and the 16 September 1922 memorandum.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks: written as a new dossier by the me-10-x additions batch (cliopatria_names []). Counterpart usage by other dossiers: state-of-israel and palestinians name the slug british-mandate-for-palestine; the french-mandate-for-syria-and-lebanon 1923-03 loss names the string 'Mandatory Palestine', which should read british-mandate-for-palestine (this dossier's gain of 1923-03 mirrors it). The east bank is deliberately outside the shape (kingdom-of-jordan founds Transjordan in April 1921 from nobody); the 16 September 1922 memorandum is recorded in the keyframe notes and sources, not as a ledger event, because no land in this shape changed hands. High Commissioners: the page lists only Herbert Samuel (1920-1925) and Alan Cunningham (1945-1948), so identity.rulers is omitted. Not opened (page budget): the Arab revolt of 1936-1939, the 1939 White Paper, the Jewish insurgency, the Sinai/Negev frontier of 1906/1922 and the Hula Valley (Mandatory Palestine page silent on the Hula). Wikidata id left null (Cliopatria has no row; wikidata.org unreachable). Region names used all resolve in the gazetteer (Israel, Palestine, Golan, Sea of Galilee, West Bank, Gaza Strip).
